title: Finite semigroup-dressed Petz collar discriminator
question: Does a rank-preserving heat-semigroup collar give a finite, dimension-safe normalized-filter and Petz transport interface that is more stable than a hard spectral projector?
method: Shift every finite local core Hamiltonian by its spectral minimum and construct F_s=exp(-s K_A/2) for s in {1/8,1/4,1/2,1,2}.
Normalize the filtered state by m_s, test positivity and the exact mass inequality 1-m_s <= s Tr(rho K_A), and retain the measured local first moment rather than assuming a uniform bound.
Build one Petz map from the filtered B and BC marginals and reuse the R-396 contractivity and displacement triangle on both filtered and original inputs.
Record source, orientation, core, buffer, beta, scale and adjacent-cutoff profiles on a bounded pilot grid.
Run a non-importing independent lane, a Lean scalar cross-check, and hostile mutations for normalization, hard projection, one-leg exponent and omitted displacement terms.
finding: The primary lane passes 473/473 assertions over 5 systems, 12 tripartitions and 120 rows; the independent lane passes 6/6, hostile 6/6, integrated 23/23 and Lean R397 compiles. The semigroup residual is 9.81218636736738e-16. The smallest filtered mass is 0.344378492577764, the maximum mass defect is 0.655621507422236, and the first-moment mass slack is at least 0.0030674280806310544. The tested normalized-filter candidate envelope sqrt(1-m_s)+(1-m_s)/2 has minimum slack 0.2037704602201066. Projected and transported Petz errors peak at 0.010367294505488315 and 0.01058510613640556; all finite violations are zero. The maximum adjacent-cutoff transport ratio is 2.192041611389991.
decision_reason: The smooth collar survives the finite and hostile checks and lowers the observed adjacent-cutoff transport ratio relative to R-396, so the route advances as a finite interface. The mass and candidate envelope remain scale- and cutoff-dependent, and the pilot does not prove a cutoff-independent moment or a common form core. The route therefore advances only to the next moment/core gate, with no claim or tier promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite semigroup collar only. It proves no dimension-safe normalized-filter theorem, cutoff/source/volume/shape uniformity, QCMI upper bound, shell summability, common core, Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, Lorentzian continuation, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
next_action: Derive or disprove a cutoff-independent local first-moment bound on a declared common core, then prove the normalized-filter modulus there and repeat the collar transport over increasing oscillator cutoffs before any Q3LOCK promotion.

adversarial_review.check: The hostile raw-state trace gap is 0.4063588377792221, so dropping m_s is caught; a uniform lower mass is not inferred.
The one-leg exponential mutation has residual 0.3341273059636541 and hard-projector substitution residual 0.5895002061771643.
Dropping both displacement terms is caught because 0.006145099757872087 exceeds 0.004143142716819127 while the genuine budget remains valid.
The maximum adjacent-cutoff transport ratio is 2.192041611389991 on the pilot, so the profile is not promoted to a uniform bound.
The mass inequality uses the measured moment, whose cutoff-independent control and common form-core embedding remain unproved.
Semigroup composition is an Euclidean collar identity and is not a causal cone or physical-time generator.
